review: Review-3 follow-up: coalesce RunStore submit wakeups so large batches do not accumulate stale notifications

fix.finding: FileRunStore.Release() ran on every Submit (including idempotent replays) while the worker only waits when no work is available, so a large batch left one stale semaphore permit per Submit. After the batch drained, the worker performed that many unnecessary TryClaim calls (store-lock acquisitions and pending-index reads) before blocking again.
fix.change: The work signal is now a capacity-one SemaphoreSlim. Submit (and replay) call SignalSubmittedWork(), which coalesces a burst into at most one pending wakeup (SemaphoreFullException is swallowed). WaitForWorkAsync returns bool (true = notification consumed, false = timeout). The durable pending index remains the source of truth; the worker's 1 s timeout fallback still covers cross-process submits and expired leases.
tests: Batched_submits_leave_at_most_one_pending_wakeup: 20 submissions, then process all work without waiting; after the batch the worker performs at most 2 consecutive empty claims (old design allowed one per historical Submit).
Repeated_idempotent_submits_coalesce_into_one_wakeup: 10 replays of the same idempotency key leave exactly one wakeup; the next wait times out.
Existing WaitForWorkAsync wake/timeout/cancellation tests remain green.

measured.staleWakeupsBefore: up to 1 per Submit (20 for the test batch; 10,000 for a 10,000-Run batch)
measured.staleWakeupsAfter: at most 1 outstanding notification (1-2 consecutive empty claims incl. the current poll)
measured.scope: Submit work-signal only; claim/complete/lease semantics unchanged.

browserEvidence.status: not re-run for review-3: the change is backend-only (FileRunStore / SimulationWorker); no frontend or rendering code changed.
browserEvidence.reference: docs/evidence/perf-2026-10-27-review2.json (600-frame dev/60 Hz WebGPU gates, Worker 500/2000/5000 stress, RunStore 10k benchmark).

knownBoundaries: Steady-state Submit is O(entries in its idempotency shard) — roughly 1/256 of idempotency records under uniform hashing — not strictly O(1); the single-file index it replaced was O(R) per Submit.
The first Submit after process start still pays the one-time O(R) reconciliation + shard rebuild on the worker-startup path (RecoverIndexes), about 2.0 s at 10,000 historical Runs.
Telemetry pending-frame merge is entity-level (full numeric record per entityId); field-level delta semantics are not defined.
The product render path consumes 16 telemetry slots; the 5000-entity Worker stress validates Worker throughput/memory only, not an end-to-end 5000-device business path.
Browser gate numbers remain single-machine headless Chrome baselines and are not part of this backend-only verification.
